questions.passage:
A: »_____ heißen Sie?«
B: »Ich heiße Maria Weber.«
questions.explanationEnglish: 'Wie heißen Sie?' literally 'How are you called?' — the standard way to ask a name.

concept.title: Wie fragt nach Zuständigkeit
concept.rule: 'Wie' asks about manner or identity: wie heißen, wie alt, wie bitte. 'Woher' asks origin, 'Was' asks for a thing.
concept.exampleGerman: Wie heißen Sie? — Ich heiße Maria.
concept.exampleEnglish: What's your name? — My name is Maria.

questions.explanationEnglish: V2: the conjugated verb 'komme' must occupy position 2.

concept.title: V2 — Verb an Position 2
concept.rule: In German statements the conjugated verb is always the second element. Whatever fills position 1, the verb follows immediately.
concept.exampleEnglish: Today I live in Berlin. (verb still second!)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct ending for formal 'Sie':
questions.explanationEnglish: Formal 'Sie' takes the infinitive -en ending: 'wohnen Sie'.

concept.title: Formal Sie = infinitive form
concept.rule: The formal 'Sie' conjugates exactly like 'sie' (they): base verb + en. Always capitalized.
concept.exampleGerman: Wo wohnen Sie? — Ich wohne in Wien.
concept.exampleEnglish: Where do you live? — I live in Vienna.

questions.explanationEnglish: German 'ei' is always the 'eye' sound. 'ie' is the 'ee' sound.

concept.title: ei = eye, ie = ee
concept.rule: When e and i go walking, the LAST letter talks: 'ei' → [aɪ] (eye), 'ie' → [iː] (ee).
